note: Presets are saved parameter sets for the same animation; they do not count as additional animations. All content is fictional and illustrative (jurisdiction unspecified). The total and every value are hypothetical placeholders labelled as such. One supplied datum is replaced by the alternative datum supplied in the preset; only that piece's length changes and the old value stays traceable. No share rule or legal doctrine is stated and nothing is attributed, ranked or decided. Long-labels-stress: coordinator decision (standing stress-cap rule, docs/AUTHORING.md item 20, from LAW-0687/0689–0692; scene-area floor >= 0.20 of the frame as in accepted LAW-0701/0705, lens >= 0.35 of the frame's short side). True driver: the 1:1 box — the scene (rail, shelf, trays, floor) must cover >= 0.20 of the frame area while a lens of >= 0.35 of the short side opens beside or above it and every text stays >= 16 px. Fallbacks tried: the lens to the right, below or over the rack; the panel beside (five widths) or below (two chips a row); compact rail zones; staggered value chips; only the focus tray's value chip (the other values listed in the allocation chips); two-line focus chips. Measured, rendered at 1080p (2026-10-05; pre-cap copy production/scratch/causation-10/LAW-0720.stress-precap.json): full counts (four events, two totals described, two accounts put forward, one labelled connector) → 1:1 scene area 0.045 (S 60); one total, one account, no connector note → 0.065; no account → 0.081. The stress therefore caps the counts at three events (the first three), one total described, no account put forward and no connector note (baseline 3 / 1 / 0 / 0); every text field keeps its near-maximum length. After the cap: 1:1 16 px, area 0.214; 9:16 0.369; 16:9 0.257.
